title: Sum of Matrix After Queries
summary: Given an integer n and a 2D array queries, initially create an n x n matrix filled with zeros.
statement: Given an integer n and a 2D array queries, initially create an n x n matrix filled with zeros. For each query, if the type is 0, update the entire row at the specified index with the given value. If the type is 1, update the entire column at the specified index with the given value. After applying all queries, return the sum of all elements in the matrix.
constraints: Begin with an n by n matrix of zeroes.
A query [0,i,v] assigns v to every cell in row i; [1,i,v] does the same for column i.
Apply queries in order and return the final sum of all cells.
hints: Process queries backward so the first unseen assignment is each row or column’s final one.
Track rows and columns already fixed by later queries.
A new row contributes value times the number of unfixed columns, and symmetrically for a column.
Every final cell is counted exactly when the later of its row and column assignments is encountered in reverse.
editorial: Every final cell is counted exactly when the later of its row and column assignments is encountered in reverse.

tests.explanation: After all overwrites the rows are [4,1,2], [4,0,2], and [4,3,3], totaling twenty-three.
The later row assignment overwrites the earlier one, leaving row zero sum two.
